diagnosis: The secret rotation endpoint retrieves ExternalIntegration by integration_id and assigns a new secret token, returning it in the HTTP response. Because it lacks tenant scoping against request.auth.organization_id, an attacker can rotate API secrets for third-party integrations belonging to other organizations, locking them out and obtaining valid credentials.

corrected_code:
from ninja import Router
from ninja.security import HttpBearer
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
import secrets
from .models import ExternalIntegration

router = Router(auth=HttpBearer())

@router.post("/integrations/{integration_id}/rotate-secret")
def rotate_integration_secret(request, integration_id: int):
    integration = get_object_or_404(
        ExternalIntegration,
        id=integration_id,
        organization=request.auth.organization
    )
    new_secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    integration.api_secret = new_secret
    integration.save(update_fields=["api_secret"])
    return {"integration_id": integration.id, "new_secret": new_secret}
